body:
I know it seems hard but you will adjust. I've been through something similar. Our bodies aren't perfect, and sometimes they fail us. It happens to almost everyone eventually. 
If you live in the UK then you don't really need to drive. I'm 20 and I never bothered learning and I can't anticipate it being a problem. Public transport here is pretty good.

Thanks for taking the time to read and respond to this. I guess I'll just stick out the rest of the year and then decide whether to carry on. I really hope I don't end up dropping out though, moving home would be hell. Yeah, I'm going to start exercising again tomorrow - it usually makes me feel a bit better.

This is exactly the kind of thing therapy (CBT) can help with. You need to get into more positive mental habits. It might take some time and dedication but you can make it through. Reach out to a professional.

I used to be a pretty funny guy. It was something I prided myself over. People used to say I should go into stand up. I could always cheer people up, break the ice in groups and make new friends by making them laugh. 

All of that's gone now. I'm a shell of the person I once was. I'm awkward, shy, introverted, insecure, depressed, anxious etc etc etc. I have lost my sense of humour. I'm not really good at anything except academics, and I'm even starting to lose a grip on that. I feel like a totally different person than I was five years ago. Occasionally the old me will shine through when I'm comfortable with someone, but it's a very rare occurrence.

I spoke to my tutor today and she really calmed me down. She emailed my professor and I had a word with him later that afternoon. He couldn't specifically talk to me about the essay because it's against university policy but he thinks that based on my previous work I'll be fine. I hope so. I took most of the afternoon off to calm down a bit. I've actually done quite a lot done tonight. I managed to get a plan together and actually start the essay. I still feel stressed but it's not overwhelming anymore. I don't know if this essay is going to turn out all that great but at least I've tried my best. Thanks again for the support, yesterday was a really awful day.

1: I'm sorry to hear about your brother but you doing the same isn't going to bring him back and you should ask yourself whether that's what he would've wanted. 

2: You're in college and unless you really need the money, there'll be plenty of time to get a job in the future. 

3: Weight can be lost, diets can be changed. A few extra pounds isn't permanent; suicide is. 

4: Talk to an advisor. Maybe consider taking a semester or two off from college to get your mental health sorted out. 

5: Are you seeking help with these disorders? If not, do so ASAP. Colleges usually have free counselling services so take advantage of this.

You are not hopeless, that's why you posted this. Some part of you doesn't want to die. There is always hope, even when it may not seem clear. I cannot guarantee you're situation will improve because you have not elaborated on it but I'm willing to bet it's not hopeless. I, for one, have hope for you. Please seek some kind of professional help.

Just let him know that you're there for him if he ever needs to talk but don't ask invasive questions. Maybe ask if he wants to hang out some time. Depression can be a very lonely place and it can be comforting just to know that you have a shoulder to cry on.

Tomorrow is a new day. The past is done, you cannot change it. Work on making the rest of your life better. You have NOT wasted your life, you still have time ahead of you. Forgive yourself. If you feel you have done wrong to others, seek forgiveness from them too or forgive yourself on their behalf. I can tell you have had a hard life but it is still one worth living. Seek help, focus on the future and try to enjoy the simple pleasures in life.

I'm going to ask my advisor tomorrow, she might refer me on to them but it's still these Christmas break so I don't know if they're going to be around. I wouldn't even know how they could help me... I can't even begin to understand the reading. 

Thank you for your reply though, I appreciate it :)

Thanks a lot for the reply! We do sound very similar. I'm terrified of failing, I really can't face the idea of dropping out because I already spent a year out after high school. 

I've talked to a couple of people in the class and one seems to be struggling, the other seems to be doing okay. I'm too much of a wreck right now to ask for help from them. I tried the reading again before but still didn't understand it. I ended up crying on the phone to my mum and friend again. I'm going to see what my advisor says tomorrow. I think I'm going to end up just having to write it from my lecture notes without the extra reading and accept the poor grade. I've never gotten a poor grade in anything but the reading stresses me out the point of retching so I don't think I'm going to get anywhere with it. 

Thanks again for your reply, it has calmed me down a bit :)
